rationale: Both candidates independently rediscovered the review's central surviving concern — the MiniMax-H3 default rel_l1_thresh silently staying at 0.2 because async_omni_engine injects it before the None-sentinel model-default logic runs — and both correctly validated that the partition-gated enabler (GT concern 1) is already fixed; neither flagged the offline-example variable issue or the two inline extractor/test bugs (all apparently already resolved by the time of this diff, so the miss is low-cost). Y's write-up is more rigorous, executing code to confirm the threshold bug and adding genuinely new, well-grounded findings (memory footprint scaling, wasted RoPE computation on cached steps, a cache-hit test that can't detect a stale-timestep bug) that mirror the ground-truth reviewer's own verify-by-running methodology. X contributes one distinct high-value catch (Cache-DiT/TeaCache stacking under quality=high) but pads its list with three overlapping AMD-CI-coverage findings that add little beyond the first.
